headline: High: aci’s broad egress and shared API/MCP-style integrations create default leakage and cascading-action risk when paired with local-only langchain4j.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest content through direct function calls or an MCP server, and langchain4j is a framework that can be used to pass model outputs into downstream prompts. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so the interaction is inferred; uncertainty pushes this above low. The pathway exists if aci outputs are fed into langchain4j without sanitization.
conditions: IF aci outputs are copied into langchain4j prompts or tools without filtering, injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP or message channel is introduced between the pair, attacker-controlled content can bridge them.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and instruction/content split before passing aci output onward.
Strip tool directives and markdown from aci outputs before reuse.
Review one sample handoff for prompt-injection markers.
Disable any shared MCP bridge unless provenance tagging is added.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; langchain4j is a framework that can route data to model backends. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive work data if aci-fed content is forwarded into langchain4j or its model calls. The evidence is indirect, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF aci data is forwarded into langchain4j prompts or embeddings, sensitive CRM/email/calendar content may leave the local boundary.
IF langchain4j is configured with a remote model backend, forwarded content can be transmitted off-host.
mitigations: Minimize fields sent from aci to langchain4j.
Redact email, CRM, and calendar identifiers before handoff.
Use a local model backend for langchain4j.
Audit one end-to-end request for outbound payloads.
requires-engineering: add data-class allowlists at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API writes, while langchain4j itself is a framework with no explicit write surface in the profile. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope, so only a limited conflict risk is visible. Uncertainty remains because aci’s integrations could overlap with a langchain4j-driven workflow if configured that way.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API object, conflicting updates can occur.
IF aci is run in parallel instances against the same CRM record, last-write-wins races are possible.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each resource.
Serialize writes to shared CRM or calendar records.
Turn on per-record locking where available.
Check for duplicate updates after a test run.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency tokens to shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and langchain4j can be used to consume those outputs in downstream agent logic. No verification step is documented between them, so A’s output could become B’s input and then drive actions or responses. Because the exact orchestration is not documented, I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF langchain4j consumes aci-generated text as authoritative context, errors can cascade.
IF downstream code triggers emails, tickets, or CRM updates from that text, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Insert a human review step for any aci-derived action.
Require structured outputs with schema validation.
Compare aci claims against source records before acting.
Log one full chain from input to action for review.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: aci explicitly touches email, CRM, calendar, support, and research data, while langchain4j is a general framework with no residency or retention controls documented here. The pair therefore creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated or customer data is routed through langchain4j-backed processing. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the interaction, not aci alone.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is processed by a langchain4j deployment with different retention or residency rules, compliance gaps arise.
IF logs retain prompts or outputs longer than the source system, subject-rights handling can diverge.
mitigations: Classify the data before any handoff.
Disable prompt logging for sensitive flows.
Confirm retention settings on the langchain4j deployment.
Route regulated data only through approved backends.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared data-handling policy.
